item.title: AI Investment Boom Faces Reality Check From Markets and Regulators
item.description: After months of asking who can spend the most, investors are increasingly asking a different question.

item.title: Markets Brace for One of the Most Uncertain Fed Days in Years
item.description: A chorus of investors say a rate hike is in the cards.

item.title: Hermès’ Chief Tracks China’s Pork Prices to Gauge Handbag Market
item.description: When it comes to gauging the possibility of a sales rebound for his luxury group in China, Hermès Executive Chairman Axel Dumas turns to an unusual metric: pork prices.

item.title: Irish Economy Rebounds With 3.9% Growth After Early-Year Slump
item.description: Ireland’s economy rebounded following a slump at the start of the year, while Belgium failed to grow, offering mixed signals for the euro zone as it grapples with the fallout from the Iran war.

item.title: Nvidia Partner Quanta Seeks Up to $2.2 Billion From Offering
item.description: Artificial-intelligence server maker Quanta Computer Inc. is seeking to raise as much as $2.19 billion from a sale of global depositary shares, in an offering that may be the biggest Taiwanese stock sale in 19 years.

item.title: Ares $29 Billion Private Credit Fund Sees Uptick in Non-Accruals
item.description: Ares Management Corp.’s $29 billion flagship private credit fund reported an increase in troubled investments in the second quarter, as the industry continues to grapple with exposure to businesses vulnerable to advances in artificial intelligence.

item.title: DJI Debuts Long-Awaited Osmo 4P Camera, But US Creators Can’t Buy It
item.description: Chinese drone maker DJI is rolling out its latest product, a $700 mechanically stabilized camera, pressing ahead with global launches while its products remain locked out of the US market following a federal ban last year.

item.title: Aramco Mulls New Oil Pricing for Asia as Houthis Threaten Flows
item.description: Saudi Aramco is preparing a new selling price for oil loaded at Egypt’s Mediterranean port of Sidi Kerir for delivery to Asia after attacks by Iran-backed Houthi militants elevated risks in the Red Sea.

item.title: EU Will Support Cities That Want to Curb Short-Term Rentals
item.description: The European Union is preparing measures that will help cities clamp down on short-term rental operators like Airbnb, as Brussels aims to tackle the problem of housing affordability and supply.

item.title: ‘Mr. Brexit’ Leaves Mizuho and UK After Running FICC Strategy
item.description: Jordan Rochester, who made his name as one of the UK’s most recognized financial commentators during the country’s split from the European Union, has left Mizuho Bank Ltd. to pursue a position overseas.

item.title: ASMPT Chief Sees AI Equipment Demand Intact as Bubble Fears Rise
item.description: Chip gear maker ASMPT Ltd.’s top boss said that long-term demand for AI-driven equipment remains firmly intact, pushing back against against growing investor fears of an AI bubble.

item.title: Ukraine Says It Hit Major Rosneft Refinery in Russia’s Ryazan
item.description: Ukraine says it attacked a refinery owned by Russia’s largest oil producer Rosneft PJSC overnight, its first strike on a major oil-processing facility in nearly two weeks.

item.title: Microsoft, Meta Earnings Face a Market Growing Skeptical of AI
item.description: Microsoft Corp. and Meta Platforms Inc. are about to test investors’ diminishing patience for Big Tech’s profligate spending on artificial intelligence and the dwindling cash positions that are the result of it.

item.title: Turkey Lifts Milling Wheat Export Ban as Record Harvest Expected
item.description: The Turkish government gave the green light to milling wheat exports after a year-and-a-half pause.

item.title: Adani Flagship Swings to a Loss on One-Off Cost on US Settlement
item.description: Adani Enterprises Ltd. swung to a loss in the June quarter, after booking a one-time charge for a US sanctions probe settlement that overshadowed operational strength.

item.title: Top Off-Grid Solar Firm Targets 1.5 Million Malagasy Customers
item.description: Sun King, the world’s largest off-grid solar company, plans to sell products in Madagascar and targets connecting 1.5 million customers by 2030.

item.title: Emerging-Market Stocks Sink Further as Asian Tech Slide Deepens
item.description: Emerging-market stocks plunged for a second straight day, with the benchmark gauge sinking to a three-and-a-half month low as a rout in Asian chip stocks deepened.

item.title: Schneider Electric in Talks to Buy Smart Device Maker Shelly
item.description: Schneider Electric SE is in talks to acquire Shelly Group SE, a maker of smart devices for the home, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: ING Nears SRTs on $10 Billion of Loans Including AI-Linked Debt
item.description: ING Groep NV is hedging credit risk on about $10 billion of loans via significant risk transfers as banks worldwide bolster their use of the instruments to free up capacity for new lending.

item.title: UK Mortgage Approvals Recovered in June, BOE Data Shows
item.description: UK mortgage approvals ticked up in June, with the housing market showing some resilience in the face of higher borrowing costs and political turbulence.

item.title: Singapore Upsizes Support Package to $1.5 Billion Amid Oil Shock
item.description: Singapore is nearly doubling its support package to help households and businesses defray higher costs caused by a protracted Middle East conflict.

item.title: Moonshot AI Surpasses Funding Goal to Hit $35 Billion Value
item.description: Moonshot AI secured a $35 billion valuation after raising a larger-than-anticipated $3.5 billion in a just-closed round of financing, riding the momentum from a breakthrough Kimi K3 model that sent ripples through Silicon Valley.

item.title: Euro-Zone Wage Growth Set to Quicken Into 2027, ECB Says
item.description: Euro-area pay growth is poised to accelerate through early 2027, though will remain far below previous peaks, the European Central Bank said as it gauges inflation resulting from the Iran war.

item.title: CVC Is Said to Consider Sale of Chinese Pharmacy Chain Yikang
item.description: CVC Capital Partners Plc is considering a sale of its Chinese retail pharmacy chain Xi’an Yikang Pharmaceutical Co., according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Advantest Lifts Outlook After AI Chip Tester Demand Soars
item.description: Advantest Corp. raised its outlook above estimates, pointing to robust demand for testers needed to manufacture increasingly complex chips for AI data centers.

item.title: India to Push Tax Bill For Global Bond Funds Amid Parliament Din
item.description: India’s government expects Parliament to pass a bill that formalizes tax cuts for foreign investors buying its sovereign debt, according to people with knowledge of the matter, betting the legislation’s bipartisan nature will cut through other contentious debates.

item.title: AI Stock Selloff Accelerates as Investors Rotate Out of Chip Winners
item.description: After piling into chip stocks and so-called AI winners, investors are now rushing to cut this exposure and rebalance portfolios. Even allowing for that, an acceleration of the selloff in recent days over China competitive risks looks premature.

item.title: Valterra Platinum Dividend Surges 29-Fold After Prices Jump
item.description: Valterra Platinum Ltd. hiked its interim dividend almost 29-fold as the payout beat analyst expectations.

item.title: Legrand Lifts Outlook as Clients Pour Billions Into Data Centers
item.description: Legrand SA boosted its sales guidance as customers continue to invest heavily in artificial intelligence infrastructure.
